purpose: Close #4683 by correcting the one thing in it that is still wrong. The versioned scrypt scheme, the legacy bcrypt verify and the opportunistic atomic upgrade all landed (#4684, #4822), but the module's documented storage format stayed on n=65536 after the profile moved to the OWASP n=131072 rung. The comment therefore described a format the module never writes, and a parser built from it would reject every real hash.
requiredInvariants: No behaviour changes. PASSWORD_SCRYPT_PARAMS stays at the OWASP N=2^17, r=8, p=1 rung chosen in #4684 after the load/DoS measurement; PASSWORD_BCRYPT_COST stays 12; the encoder, the parser and the upgrade path are untouched. The only executable change is an added test.
The dummy-hash timing-oracle set is neither weakened nor removed, and DUMMY_PASSWORD_HASH stays on bcrypt so both login branches keep doing comparable work for the existing population.
The password policy (12-128, character classes) is not touched - that is V6.2.5 and it sits behind an owner blocker on breach lists.
No schema change, no migration, no new dependency, no lockfile change. passwordHash remains a plain String column.
No production, REG.RU, DNS, database or credential mutation. New mandatory cost: 0 RUB.
acceptance: The staleness was measured, not assumed: hashPassword() emits $scrypt$v=1$n=131072,r=8,p=1$... while the docstring documented $scrypt$v=1$n=65536,r=8,p=1$...

The fix is not the corrected number. A comment corrected by hand can go stale again the same way, so the example is now bound to PASSWORD_SCRYPT_PARAMS by a test that reads the source - the same technique the existing maxmem check already uses - and is additionally checked against the prefix a real hash carries, so the assertion holds against production output and not only against a constant that could itself drift from the encoder.
password-hashing-versioned.spec.ts 41 of 41 to 42 of 42; both password suites together 51 of 51 to 52 of 52.
Mutation M1, restoring the docstring to n=65536 with the constant left alone: the new test fails, and only it.

Mutation M2, lowering the constant to N=2^16 with the docstring left alone: 3 fail, the new test among them, so the binding is two-way. Reported as 3 rather than 1 because the two pre-existing work-factor tests catch that mutation too - it does not isolate, and claiming it did would overstate the test.
